entities.text: Cholamandalam Ms General Insurance ... vs Rekha W/O. Popat Gayakwad
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Cholamandalam MS General Insurance company and the claimant have preferred this appeal and cross objection in respect of the judgment and award passed in MVC No.141/2010 on the file of Addl. MACT, Bilagi dated 11.10.2013.

2. Facts in brief which are necessary for disposal of the appeal are as under:
2.1
In the road traffic accident that occurred on 21.11.2009 involving Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-29/A- 615 and another auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-29/8178, Popat S/o Maruti Gayakwada lost his life.

Accordingly, his wife, children and other dependants have filed claim petition before the tribunal in MVC No.141/2010. 2.2 Police after thorough investigation with regard to the incident filed charge sheet against the drivers of both the auto rickshaws.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:1009 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100090 of 2023 2.3

Tribunal on contest, allowed the claim petition in part and awarded Rs.8,14,000/- as compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization holding that Cholamandalam MS General Insurance company and the owner of the auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-29/A-615 are liable to pay the compensation.
3. Being aggrieved by this Cholamandalam MS General Insurance company and claimants have preferred present appeal and cross objection.

4. Miss.Anusha Sangami, counsel representing Sri.S.K.Kayakmath contended that, when there is a charge sheet against the drivers of both the auto rickshaw and both the auto rickshaws are insured with the Cholamandalam MS General Insurance company as well as Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd.
The tribunal ought to have apportioned the compensation and fastened the liability in the ratio of 50% each on both the insurance company.
Therefore, sought for allowing the appeal by passing appropriate orders.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:1009 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100090 of 2023 5.

Whereas, Si.G.R.Turumuri, learned counsel representing claimants in the cross objection,
contended that tribunal has wrongly assessed the quantum of compensation by taking monthly income in a sum of Rs.4500/- for the accidental injuries of the year 2009 and it should have been sum of Rs.5,000/- p.m. and so also on the head loss of future income, no compensation is awarded.

6. By following the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157, United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and Others reported in AIR 2020 SC 3076 and Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram and Others reported in 2018 ACJ 2782, the claimants would be entitled for 40,000/- each towards loss of filial affection and sought for reassessment of the compensation.

sentences.text: In view of the rival contentions of the parties, Sri.Kartik Ganachari representing the Reliance insurance company however supported the impugned judgment.
8. In view of the rival contentions of the parties, this court has perused the material on record meticulously.

9. On such perusal of the material on record, in the case on hand Popat lost his life in the road traffic accident that occurred on 21.11.2009 involving auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-29/A-615 and another Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-29/8178 is not in dispute.

Admittedly, Popat was a inmate of passenger auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-29/A-615.
10.
Police after thorough investigation filed charge sheet against drivers of both the auto rickshaws.

Accordingly, tribunal has grossly erred in fastening the liability only on the driver of the auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-29/A-615.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:1009 C/W MFA.CROB No. 100090 of 2023 11.

When two charge sheets are filed by the police after thorough investigation, the tribunal was duty bound to apportion the quantum of compensation payable by both the insurance company in the ratio of 50% each.
Therefore, a case is made by the appellant in MFA No.100986/2014 for allowing the appeal, to pay to the extent of 50% of the adjudged compensation.
12. This would take us to the next question that is whether cross objector has made the accused for encashment of compensation?
13. Admittedly, claimants have failed to produced proper proof of income.

In such circumstances,
for the accident of the year 2009, quantum of compensation is to be taken into a sum of Rs.5,000 as against Rs.4,500/- taken by the tribunal.
So also on the ground of filial affection improper compensation has been awarded by the tribunal.
Therefore, a case is made out for reassessment of compensation.
The reassessment of compensation is as under; Sl
. No. Name of heads Amount(Rs.) 1 Loss of dependency 11,34,000-00 2 Loss of estate and Funeral 30,000-00 expenses 3 Loss of love and affection 2,00,000-00 Total 13,64,000-00 15.
As against sum of Rs.8,14,000/-, the claimants would be entitled for sum of Rs.13,64,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
16. Hence, the following :
